problemStatement.formal: \text{Target guarantee: } \exists S,\ \operatorname{cutWeight}(G,S) \ge \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{totalWeight}(G), with comparison to the Goemans-Williamson ratio.
problemStatement.plain: Track the basic randomized MaxCut guarantee: a random partition should cut half the total edge weight in expectation, yielding a partition with at least half the total weight, and compare that baseline with the Goemans-Williamson approximation ratio.
whyMatters: Randomized MaxCut is a clean example of the probabilistic method in approximation algorithms.
The record also documents the path from an axiomatized existence statement to the later conditional-expectations proof.

proven: `random_partition_expected_cut` records the nonnegativity sanity check for the weighted expected-cut expression used by the OQ02 setup.
`gw_ratio_lower` and `gw_beats_random` record numerical comparisons for the placeholder Goemans-Williamson ratio constant.
`max_ge_avg`, `greedyContrib_ge_half`, `sum_cutWeight_eq`, and `exists_good_partition'` in the related OQ04 file provide the deterministic averaging and conditional-expectations route.
`conditional_expectation_method` packages the fully proved constructive MaxCut baseline in the OQ04 development.
open: `exists_good_partition` is axiomatized in OQ02; the related OQ04 file removes that axiom for the constructive baseline.
The OQ02 Goemans-Williamson ratio is a placeholder constant, not a full SDP-rounding formalization.
knownResults.goal: Track the randomized half-cut guarantee and its axiom-free conditional-expectations refinement as a small approximation-algorithm case study.
